title: Sun Valley Film Festival to Open With ‘The Debut’; Honorees Announced
description: The Sun Valley Film Festival, which takes place Dec. 2 to Dec. 6 in the Idaho resort town, will open with “The Debut” and close with “Artificial.”
body:
The Sun Valley Film Festival, which takes place Dec. 2 to Dec. 6 in the Idaho resort town, will open with “The Debut” and close with “Artificial.” Jessica Lange, Bill Pullman, Seth Rogen and Lauren Miller Rogen, Stephen Beresford and Luke Davies are set to be honored by the festival, which was founded in 2012. 

	Lange (“Long Day’s Journey Into Night”) will receive the Vision Award, Pullman (“Everybody Digs Bill Evans”) the Pioneer Award and the Rogens (“Tangled”) will receive the Impact Award. Beresford (“Elsinore”) will be honored with the High Scribe Award and Davies (“Tenzing”) with the Disruptor Award. In addition, director Peter Farrelly will participate in a Q&A after a special screening of “I Play Rocky.”
	

	Also screening at this year’s festival are “All of a Sudden,” “Elsinore,” “Everybody Digs Bill Evans,” “Long Day’s Journey Into Night,” “A Long Winter,” “The Row,” “Tangles” and “Tenzing” as well as “The Caged,” “Caity,” “Go Deep: The DeSean Jackson Story,” “Jollyface,” “Moving Joy,” “Stealing Magic” and “Under Fire.”

	“This year’s lineup brings together artists who have shaped film and television across generations, from Jessica Lange and Bill Pullman to Peter Farrelly,” said Teddy Grennan, executive director and co-founder of the Sun Valley Film Festival. “Sun Valley is a place where audiences can get close to the craft, whether through a screening, a Coffee Talk or a conversation over dinner, and we’re thrilled to welcome these remarkable talents to the mountains this December.”

	 See the complete schedule at sunvalleyfilmfestival.org.

schema.headline: Sun Valley Film Festival to Open With ‘The Debut’; Honorees Announced

title: Gang Dong-won, Kim Go-eun to Star in Netflix’s ‘The Twilight Between Us’ From ‘When Life Gives You Tangerines’ Director, ‘Queen of Tears’ Writer
description: Netflix has set Gang Dong-won and Kim Go-eun to play heirs to two feuding houses who are married off by order of the king in “The Twilight Between
body:
Netflix has set Gang Dong-won and Kim Go-eun to play heirs to two feuding houses who are married off by order of the king in “The Twilight Between Us,” a romance-action period drama directed by Kim Won-suk (“When Life Gives You Tangerines”) and written by Park Ji-eun (“Queen of Tears”).

	The series follows Mu-yeong and Su-ryeon, whose families have been feuding for a century. The king arranges the match in the hope of finally ending the hostility between the two clans. The marriage does not go to plan, and soon heads somewhere no one saw coming.
	

	Gang plays Mu-yeong, an illegitimate son of the House of Kang. He is a gifted fighter with a good heart, yet he lives out of sight, weighed down by a menacing nickname: “Demon of the North.”

	Kim plays Su-ryeon, the House of Han’s only daughter. After her bid to become Crown Princess falls short, she is caught by the royal marriage ban. Being paired with Mu-yeong is a turn of fate she never expected.

	The Korean title hinges on the syllable hon, which can be read two ways. It can point to marriage, as in gyeol-hon. It can also refer to hon as twilight – the short stretch after the sun sets when it is hard to say where day stops and night starts.

	Kim Won-suk’s directing credits also include “Misaeng: Incomplete Life,” “Signal” and “My Mister.” Park’s writing credits also include “Crash Landing on You” and “Legends of the Blue Sea.” No release date has been announced.

	On the reality front, Netflix is following up “Culinary Class Wars” with “Vocal Class Wars,” a singing survival competition the streamer has greenlit for a 2027 launch.
	

	The show sets two camps against each other. On one side are the “White Singers,” well-known artists whose names are shorthand for an entire genre. On the other are the “Black Singers,” challengers who perform without their names or public personas and must earn their place on the strength of their voices alone.

	Behind the series are Kim Hak-min, who produced “Culinary Class Wars,” and Park Sung-hwan, whose credits include the beauty competition show “Just Makeup.” The pair previously worked together on “Sing Again.”

	“Following ‘Culinary Class Wars,’ we’re excited to expand the ‘black-and-white’ universe to a new stage – music,” the “Vocal Class Wars” production team said. “Watch for whether the legendary artists appearing as ‘White Singers’ can protect their reputation, or whether the ‘Black Singers’ set to shock the world will flip the script – expect another thrilling showdown and unpredictable twists in this next class war.”

schema.headline: Gang Dong-won, Kim Go-eun to Star in Netflix’s ‘The Twilight Between Us’ From ‘When Life Gives You Tangerines’ Director, ‘Queen of Tears’ Writer

title: Russell Brand’s Instagram Account Removed By Meta After Rape Conviction
description:
Russell Brand, who was convicted of rape last week in London, posted on X Wednesday that his Instagram account has been removed by Meta. 

	Brand p
body:
Russell Brand, who was convicted of rape last week in London, posted on X Wednesday that his Instagram account has been removed by Meta. 

	Brand posted a screenshot reading, “We disabled your account. Our technology found your account, or your activity on it, doesn’t follow our rules.”

	“We suspended your page. This is because Russell Brand goes against our community standards,” reads the screenshot from Brand’s now-removed Instagram profile page. 
	

	The British comedian was sentenced Monday to 10 years and six months in prison after being convicted of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. 

	Brand’s X page, with 10 million followers, is still active. “There never was a Russell Brand, according to @Meta. Thank God for @elonmusk. Stay tuned,” he wrote on X Wednesday.

	Brand’s account was taken down because it “violates our policies,” a Meta spokesperson confirmed to TMZ.

	After Brand’s comedy and movie appearances tapered off, he started a YouTube channel which during the COVID pandemic became increasingly right-wing and full of conspiracy theories.

	He was accused of sexual misconduct multiple times before finally being charged in 2025. In 2023, YouTube suspended monetization of his account. 

	Judge Joel Bennathan began his sentencing remarks Monday by saying, “About 20 years ago, Russell Brand, you were becoming famous. You were clever and, in many people’s eyes, funny and charismatic. You had also become a sexual predator.”

	“No doubt your companions thought it was outrageous laddish behavior that only you could get away with: It was outrageous and possibly laddish, but also a criminal sexual offense, and as it turns out you haven’t got away with it,” the judge noted. 
	

	London’s Metropolitan Police said that Brand is being investigated on further allegations of rape from two other women.

schema.headline: Russell Brand’s Instagram Account Removed By Meta After Rape Conviction

title: ‘Jimmy Kimmel Live’ Hits Its Highest Ratings Ever for a Midterm Election Telecast With 2.4 Million Viewers
description:
Last week’s midterm elections brought good news for more than just the Democratic party.

	The Tuesday night episode of “Jimmy Kimmel Live” brought
body:
Last week’s midterm elections brought good news for more than just the Democratic party.

	The Tuesday night episode of “Jimmy Kimmel Live” brought 2.4 million viewers to ABC, according to Nielsen. That total marks not only a 53% increase compared with the late night talk show’s most recent midterm telecast on Nov. 8, 2022, which reached 1.6 million viewers, but its biggest midterm election telecast ever. Kimmel also did well in terms of rating among adults age 18-49, scoring a 0.32 — an increase of 68% from 2022’s 0.19 rating. Excluding episodes that benefited from NFL, NBA and NHL lead-in, that’s the highest rating Kimmel has seen in more than a year, since the buzzy episode on Sept. 23, 2025 in which he returned to the air after his controversial suspension over comments he made about the assassination of Charlie Kirk.
	

	“Jimmy Kimmel Live” had a strong week overall, averaging 2.5 million viewers and a 0.23 rating among adults age 18-49 overall, bringing the show to the No. 1 position in both metrics compared with its late-night competitors. It has remained in the top spot for all seven weeks of the broadcast season thus far. 

	And when comparing with last season’s viewership, “Jimmy Kimmel Live” is showing double-digit growth. The season average to date is 2.5 million viewers, up 16% from last year’s 2.1 million viewer-average at the same point in time. This is the fifth season in a row that the show has shown year-over-year growth by Week 7 of the broadcast calendar. Season 25 is currently on track to become Kimmel’s most-watched in 12 years, since the 2014-2015 season.

schema.headline: ‘Jimmy Kimmel Live’ Hits Its Highest Ratings Ever for a Midterm Election Telecast With 2.4 Million Viewers

title: Frankie Muniz Hospitalized After Crashing Race Car at Daytona
description: “Malcolm in the Middle” star Frankie Muniz was rushed to a Florida hospital on Wednesday after he crashed during a practice lap at a Veterans Day e
body:
“Malcolm in the Middle” star Frankie Muniz was rushed to a Florida hospital on Wednesday after he crashed during a practice lap at a Veterans Day event at the Daytona International Speedway.

	Muniz, who picked up a second career as a racing driver in 2006, was scheduled to race as part of Team Air Force for Ford’s “Proud to Honor Veterans Day Classic” event on Wednesday. But during a practice lap while the track was closed to the public, according to Entertainment Tonight, Muniz crashed his car. He was later taken to a local hospital and will no longer participate in the event, according to ET.
	

	Representatives for Muniz and Ford Racing did not respond to an immediate request for comment. A Ford Racing spokesperson told People that Muniz was “taken to a local medical facility for further evaluation and is awake and alert,” but they did not provide an update on his condition.

	“Malcolm in the Middle” co-star Bryan Cranston, who joined Muniz in the show’s four-episode revival earlier this year on Disney+, was also set to appear at the event to support him, according to ET.

	Muniz has maintained his racing career even as he made small returns to acting throughout the 2020s. He participated in NASCAR’s Craftsman Truck Series for the last three consecutive seasons, filming the “Malcolm in the MIddle” revival last year around his racing schedule. He finished 25th in this year’s Craftsman series.

	“I was the first person that they ever had to work around cause normally like an actor is committed to the acting,” Muniz told Fox Sports’ Bob Pockrass last year. “But obviously I was a race car driver before they greenlit this show.”

schema.headline: Frankie Muniz Hospitalized After Crashing Race Car at Daytona

title: Jessica Chastain Returning to Broadway in New Play ‘Lost Lear’
description:
Jessica Chastain is returning to Broadway in “Lost Lear,” a play that puts a meta spin on “King Lear.” 

	Chastain was last on Broadway in “A Doll’
body:
Jessica Chastain is returning to Broadway in “Lost Lear,” a play that puts a meta spin on “King Lear.” 

	Chastain was last on Broadway in “A Doll’s House,” an acclaimed 2023 revival of the Henrik Ibsen drama; this is her first time appearing in a new show. 

	In “Lost Lear,” she will portray Joy, a middle-aged actress suffering from early onset dementia, whose one clear memory is performing in the Shakespeare classic. Chastain will star alongside Corey Stoll (“Appropriate”) and Michael Urie (“Once Upon a Mattress,” “Spamalot”), with additional casting to be announced at a later date.
	

	Dan Colley wrote the show and will direct in his Broadway debut.  Here’s the official logline: “As her grip on the present slips, Joy (Chastain), a former actress, is certain she’s back in rehearsal for ‘King Lear.’ At her care home, her nurse (Urie) takes his cues from her, stepping into whatever role she needs him to play. When her estranged son Conor (Stoll) comes to visit, he’s ready to tell his mother what he’s spent years leaving unsaid. But if he wants her to hear him, he’ll have to step into the scene. A limited event. A memory that will be impossible to leave behind.”

	“Lost Lear” will premiere next spring at the Booth Theatre, with previews beginning on March 29, 2027 ahead of opening night on April 23. It will run for a limited 16-week engagement. The play was first workshopped and performed in Ireland in 2022 and has since been staged in various parts of the world, including New Zealand, the U.S., the U.K., Poland and Scotland.

	“I never imagined, when we first made ‘Lost Lear,’ that it would one day be on Broadway — and I’ve imagined some pretty wild things,” Colley said. “I’m so thrilled to have the opportunity to share this piece with New York audiences and to discover new facets of the work through collaborating with this remarkable company of artists.”

schema.headline: Jessica Chastain Returning to Broadway in New Play ‘Lost Lear’

title: Tarantino Fired Mélanie Laurent From ‘Inglourious Basterds’ After ‘Terrible’ Table Read and Axed Isabelle Huppert for Not Showing Up: ‘I Don’t Owe You Jack S—‘
description: Quentin Tarantino gets brutally honest in Jay Glennie’s new book, “The Making of Quentin Tarantino’s Inglourious Basterds,” about his decision to f
body:
Quentin Tarantino gets brutally honest in Jay Glennie’s new book, “The Making of Quentin Tarantino’s Inglourious Basterds,” about his decision to fire Mélanie Laurent and Isabelle Huppert before production started on his 2009 revisionist World War II movie. Laurent ended up being rehired for the leading role of Shosanna Dreyfus, a French cinema owner seeking revenge against the Nazi officer who killed her family. 

	“Mélanie Laurent’s table read was terrible. It wasn’t good enough to be terrible,” Tarantino told the author  (via People). “The most exciting day of preproduction is for me the table read. That is the closest I get to seeing the movie for the first time. Up until then, it’s just been me reading all the scenes to myself or to a friend … so a table read with the whole cast is so exciting and so important to me. Well, Mélanie was terrible, so I fired her.”
	

	Laurent called Tarantino days after the table read to get her job back. She told the director she was not feeling well at the time and that she planned to fly herself back to Germany and put herself up at a hotel in order to read for him again. Tarantino admired Laurent’s passion and agreed to “turn the clock back” and “return to square one” with her as long as she was willing to go through three days of rehearsal with him. Whatever Laurent did doing those fateful few days impressed Tarantino enough for him to give the role of Shosanna back to her.

	“Let me just go on the record for everybody to know: I love Mélanie,” Tarantino said. “The fact of the matter is, if we were not talking about the making of ‘Inglourious Basterds,’ I would never think about the table read again for the simple reason Mélanie is my Shosanna. She did a wonderful job. But we have decided to dive deep into the making of the movie with this book, and this is an important part of its history. You know, we agreed, warts and all. So, if we had not agreed to talk about the shooting of the movie, it would be out of my mind, and I would never think about it again.”
	

	Isabelle Huppert, however, was not so lucky. She was fired by Tarantino and her role of Madame Ada Mimieux, a woman who shelters Shosanna in Paris, was given to the iconic “In the Mood for Love” star Maggie Cheung. Huppert “didn’t show up” to the table read, Tarantino said. “So fuck it. I fired her. I mean, I love Isabelle Huppert — ‘Heaven’s Gate’ and all that — but there were issues with her contract. It just kept stalling. And then not coming to the table read. Well, we cast Maggie instead.”

	“That invariably happens,” the director continued. “As far as I’m concerned, if you’re cast and you are not at that table, I don’t owe you jack shit! You can be fired, especially if I get excited by what somebody else did in your absence.” 

	Unfortunately, all of the scenes that included Madame Ada Mimieux were cut out of the movie because Tarantino felt they over-explained things too much to the audience. As the director said: “Maggie was fantastic in the movie, but you just didn’t need to know how Shosanna acquired the cinema. All we needed was a title card saying ‘Four Years Later’ and Shosanna explaining that she inherited it from her aunt.” 

	“Inglourious Basterds” world premiered at the Cannes Film Festival in May 2009, where it won best actor honors for Christoph Waltz, and then opened in theaters that August, where it became a box office hit with $321 million worldwide. The film remains one of Laurent’s signature roles. 

	“I have no moral compass when it comes to giving roles to actors: They have to be right. They have to feel like they are right for the world I have created,” Tarantino said about his freewheeling approach to hiring and firing actors. “I have fired actors in the past. If it’s not right, it is not right. I don’t owe them shit. I owe my film the best actors I can find. Period.”

	“The Making of Quentin Tarantino’s Inglourious Basterds” is now available for purchase.

schema.headline: Tarantino Fired Mélanie Laurent From ‘Inglourious Basterds’ After ‘Terrible’ Table Read and Axed Isabelle Huppert for Not Showing Up: ‘I Don’t Owe You Jack S—‘

title: Willie Nelson Says He Asked His Wife ‘To Let Me Die’ While Battling COVID: ‘All I Can Remember Is Feeling Excruciating Pain’
description: Willie Nelson is recounting a 2022 case of COVID that left him asking his wife, Annie D’Angelo, to “let me die.” The country musician recalls the e
body:
Willie Nelson is recounting a 2022 case of COVID that left him asking his wife, Annie D’Angelo, to “let me die.” The country musician recalls the experience in his new book, “The Last Leaf: Reflections on Late-Life Creativity — and My Longest Love Affair,” an excerpt of which was published by People.

	“I had the nebulizer on you, and a Q-tip up your nose to test for COVID-19,” D’Angelo wrote. (Given Nelson doesn’t remember much of the bout, he quotes his wife in the book.) “I got the oxygen going to keep you breathing, but it wasn’t working. You still couldn’t breathe. The COVID-19 test came up positive. I knew not to panic, but I also knew this was bad… In the back of the bus, you stayed isolated and grew sicker. I wasn’t sure you would make it. I alerted Dr. Greenwood that we were on our way and asked to have a mobile monoclonal antibody guy meet us at the cabin.”
	

	She continued: “Meanwhile, you got sicker with every passing hour. Every labored breath caused you incredible pain. I wanted to do more, but I’d done all I could. I just had to sit there and watch you suffer. It was the worst thing I’ve ever had to do.”

	Nelson wrote that “all I can remember is feeling excruciating pain in every cell of my body. Am I right in remembering that I said, ‘Annie, you need to let me go’?” “That’s just what you said,” responded D’Angelo. Instead of going to a hospital (which D’Angelo described as “not an option” given Nelson would have “no chance of privacy”), Wilson was given Paxlovid in an IV infusion, which helped with the illness. It was “two weeks of utter hell,” said D’Angelo, to which Nelson asked: “Did I ask you to let me die?” “Yup, twice,” she responded. “The whole thing was a nightmare.”
	

	Nelson and D’Angelo tied the knot in 1991 and share two sons, Lukas and Micah. Nelson’s memoir hit shelves Tuesday.

schema.headline: Willie Nelson Says He Asked His Wife ‘To Let Me Die’ While Battling COVID: ‘All I Can Remember Is Feeling Excruciating Pain’

title: ‘How to Rob a Bank’ Review: Nicholas Hoult and Zoë Kravitz Take Their Paychecks in an Annoyingly Flashy, Emotionally Turgid Influencer-Age Heist Movie
description: There’s a degree of second-hand embarrassment that comes from watching David Leitch’s Amazon-backed, influencer-age heist movie “How to Rob a Bank.
body:
There’s a degree of second-hand embarrassment that comes from watching David Leitch’s Amazon-backed, influencer-age heist movie “How to Rob a Bank.” It’s a film that bids so desperately for cultural relevance, stylistic cool and progressive brownie points that it trips on its own painstaking efforts to astoundingly lame results. What if Deadpool (Leitch directed one of those films, plus “Bullet Train” and “The Fall Guy”) broke the fourth wall to quack at us about his anti-capitalist revolt? Not that popular uprisings are evil, but this aggressively annoying, tonally berserk actioner serves mostly as a reminder that the revolution will not only be televised but digitally packaged and disseminated via the lousiest algorithm.
	

	As the title promises, YouTube-esque explainer videos featuring four gunmen in wolf masks bring the tips and tricks of bank robbing to a legion of online followers. Headed by the Marx-reading Ryan (Nicholas Hoult), the anonymous crew posts videos of their real-life exploits, with pop-up graphics flashing over blown-out Go-Pro-esque footage of their stick-em-ups and getaways. The erratic opener is one such movie-within-the-movie, passing through the stages of a heist as designed by the crafty group — two minutes at the bank, an anonymous 9/11 call about a mysterious package to divert police attention, and a speedy escape with motorbikes. All of the crew’s robberies throughout the film play out in this twitchy meta-mode, which makes for a bewildering, sloppily overloaded delivery of thrills.

	But the reason for this rather ugly framing device is that the team strives to educate the masses in the art of bankrobbing at the expense of being caught. Their Youtube channel includes direct-to-camera rants delivered by their lupine avatars that preach their screw-the-man gospel, entreating their massive following to take back what’s been denied them by the real fat cats and crooks. Most convincing is their claim that the government is too broken and incompetent to do anything about it, giving a Trump-era rationale to their ambitions. But the idea of sympathetic bank robbers flouting a system that only protects the rich and powerful isn’t particularly novel — it’s what underpins many a fine heist film. (There’s even a shoutout to “Point Break” in one scene.) Here, that messaging is spelled out in garish Jokerman typeface.
	

	As Ryan and his collaborators — wig-wearing decoy Emi (Anna Sawai), backup muscle Vince (Pete Davidson) and hacker Hugo (Rhenzy Feliz) — continue robbing banks and making content, amassing hundreds of millions of dollars along the way, FBI agent John West (a weirdly humorless John C. Reilly) recruits deadpan tech-wiz Raegan (a quirked-up Zoë Kravitz) as his sidekick. Raegan is on house arrest after creating an illegal software that can triangulate someone’s location by culling through online images, and but when John shows up at her Pittsburgh apartment — trying to ignore the Cheetos in her hair and the smell of weed — he promises to clear her charges in exchange for using her invention to track down the wolf-pack. 

	Their rapport gives the investigation a buddy-cop vibe that’s meant to be cute and breezy, but Mark Bianculli’s script relies on clunky wisecracks and labored eccentricities that flatten whatever low-bubbling chemistry the actors share. In any case, the intentionally odd pairing of pragmatic cop and stoner chick allows for thematically appropriate banter about the meaning of justice and peacekeeping in a chaotic and corrupt society.

	According to the film’s press notes, the four bankrobbers are meant to be thinly drawn, so that the audience can more easily project themselves onto their respective plights: Vince is a war veteran with a young daughter; Hugo, the son of undocumented immigrants; Ryan and Emi, college sweethearts whose baby boy lost his life when a white-collar insurance scam bankrupted the couple, leaving them unable to pay for his treatment. 

	In other words, they’re vessels for sadly familiar American grievances, though that doesn’t excuse the perfunctory nature in which their stories are mapped out — or the late-breaking revelations that drop like campy soap-operatic twists. Or the drearily drawn-out emotional reckonings that feel almost offensively unearned (and wildly undeserving of not just one but two plaintive Billie Eillish needle-drops). In fact, at two hours, the whole thing plods along interminably — and in the end, it’s even silly (or shameless) enough to make a case for its own self-importance.

schema.headline: ‘How to Rob a Bank’ Review: Nicholas Hoult and Zoë Kravitz Take Their Paychecks in an Annoyingly Flashy, Emotionally Turgid Influencer-Age Heist Movie

title: From Inde Navarrette’s Stunning 40-Carat Diamond Necklace to a Surprise Role Model Performance: Inside David Yurman’s VIP Dinner Party at Chateau Marmont
description:
Celebrity jeweler David Yurman hosted a dinner at Chateau Marmont Tuesday night to celebrate the reopening of his flagship boutique on Rodeo Drive.
Th
body:
Celebrity jeweler David Yurman hosted a dinner at Chateau Marmont Tuesday night to celebrate the reopening of his flagship boutique on Rodeo Drive.
The evening began with a cocktail hour where Inde Navarrette – wearing several David Yurman pieces, including a 50-carat diamond and 40-carat tanzanite necklace in white gold – sipped a martini and chatted with Eiza González. “Off Campus” star Stephen Kalyn posed for photos with Yurman and his artist wife Sybil before snapping some shots with his fiancée Victoria Lovatsis.
Yurman offered brief remarks during dinner. He thanked actor Neal McDonough for their friendship. Yurman recalled meeting McDonough for the first time, saying he got the same feeling he did when he met Roy Rogers at Madison Square Garden when he was just nine years old. When a guest asked what the secret was to his and Sybil’s 59-year marriage, Sybil cracked that her husband was a “good kisser.”
The evening was capped off by a surprise performance by Role Model. Yurman took to the stage at about one song in to reprimand some chatty guests who didn’t stop talking during the singer’s set. “This is absolutely disrespectful,” he said, adding, “Just be quiet and listen. Absorb the vibration. Absorb the beauty of this man.” Later, as Yurman and Sybil danced to “Sally, When the Wine Runs Out,” Navarrette, Kalyn, González, Tyriq Withers and Emily Bader applauded and cheered them on.

                          Man Files Report With Cops
                      
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            "The Real Housewives of Atlanta" star Angela Oakley is being accused of hurling a homophobic slur at a man … and harassing him for years ... TMZ has learned. 
      
    
            A man named Alexander Hines filed a police report with the Atlanta Police Department, claiming Angela has been bothering him since 2024. 
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Hines told cops Angela threatened to kill him and called him a homophobic slur -- the f-word --at an event on August 16, 2024. He said the incident went down in front of 20 people.
      

            Alexander claims Angela continued to send him harassing text messages over the next two years. He claims she sent men to his workplace to intimidate him … and then sent things about him to blogs to try to embarrass him. 
      
    
            Alexander also claims Angela had him served with fake legal papers.
      
    
            Angela's Steve Sadow tells TMZ ... "The police report purportedly filed by Alexander Hines contains a series of baseless and unfounded allegations. These bogus claims are entirely without merit and have no basis in fact or reality. Ms. Oakley categorically and unequivocally denies each and every one."
      
    
            Recently, he claims to have received anonymous text messages claiming that his family is being followed. Alexander said he is concerned given the pattern of behavior and wants the cops to investigate the matter.

title: 'Yes, Dear' Star Anthony Clark Dead at 62
description:
'Yes, Dear' Star Anthony Clark
                          Dead at 62
body:
'Yes, Dear' Star Anthony Clark
                          Dead at 62
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              November 11, 2026
                            4:47 PM PST
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Anthony Clark, the comedian and actor best known for starring in the CBS sitcom "Yes, Dear," has died, according to his former costar Mike O'Malley.
      
    
            O'Malley announced the news Wednesday on X, writing, "Anthony Clark died yesterday. He was a hilarious guy."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Mike remembered Anthony as a standout comedian who was already a big name in Boston during the mid-1990s, regularly selling out comedy shows.
      

            He recalled seeing Anthony perform with his wife, Lisa, at The Comedy Connection, saying they "laughed and laughed and laughed."
      
    
            Mike added ... "He was so unique one of those comics who is laughing along with you at the absurdity of his stories and observations. I was a fan before I was a friend."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The actor revealed he had spoken to Anthony just three weeks ago, saying the comedian had them laughing once again.
      
    
            Alongside his tribute, Mike shared throwback photos from the final episode of "Yes, Dear," which ended in 2006 after 122 episodes.
      
    
            Anthony starred as Greg Warner opposite O'Malley's Jimmy Hughes on the CBS sitcom, which ran for six seasons from 2000 to 2006.
      
    
            Anthony was 62.
      
    
            RIP
